Maddie: Heads-up — Hawthorn POC seeing inconsistent first-token times, sometimes >1.2s. Customer measures TTFT spike during ~500rps bursts. Can SEs triage? :thinking_face:
Kai: can you drop the request id and model + route? Did they pin a variant? Also what's their prefill/prefetch settings?
Maddie: route: /v1/generate, model: open_llama-3b, variant: quant-a1, req id: r_20260318_0923
Maddie: they use prefill=true with batch_window_ms=20 (default) and prefill_tokens=32
Ben: odd — batch_window 20ms + prefill 32 should be ok at that QPS. Do you have any logs showing KV cache misses or 429s?
Maddie: attaching log snippet below
Maddie: ```
[2026-03-18T09:23:12.345Z] req=r_20260318_0923 route=/v1/generate lat_ms=1234 tokens=12 kv_hit=false batch_size=1 shard=shard-7
[2026-03-18T09:23:12.567Z] req=r_20260318_0924 route=/v1/generate lat_ms=45 tokens=70 kv_hit=true batch_size=16 shard=shard-2
[2026-03-18T09:23:13.112Z] req=r_20260318_0925 route=/v1/generate lat_ms=1100 tokens=10 kv_hit=false batch_size=1 shard=shard-9
```
Kai: KV hit=false on slow ones = likely cache miss due to shard affinity. Are they stuck on random routing? Check routing policy: round_robin vs token_affinity.
Li: @Kai looking — our metrics show shard-7 has high cold-miss rate and is serving different model variants. Possibly stale prefill/kv layout. Suggest run `redwoodctl debug kv-stats --shard shard-7 --last 1h`
Ben: Also confirm their request pinning. If their client uses sticky session=off we may send prefill to different shard than followup tokens -> misses.
Maddie: running now… output below
Maddie: ```
$ redwoodctl debug kv-stats --shard shard-7 --last 1h
kv_hits: 18%
kv_misses: 82%
avg_kv_latency_ms: 6.2
active_variants: [quant-a1, quant-a2]
```
Li: 18% hit rate explains it. Fix options: 1) enable per-client affinity (recommended) 2) increase prefill_tokens to 128 for this workload 3) route by model-variant to avoid cross-variant placement.
Kai: For immediate mitigation, enable fallback to warm variant or increase batch_window to 50ms to allow more batching — helps amortize first-token cost.
Maddie: customer also asking about pricing if we recommend Dedicated to hit SLA. They want delta vs hosted unit cost.
Ben: ping @pricing — rough calc: Dedicated reserved capacity likely needed at sustained 500rps for 3b model. We'll ballpark — I'll DM finance and paste numbers.
Ops-bot: deploy: autoscale policy change applied to pool hawthorn-pool, add_capacity=2 gpus (rolling) :gear:
Li: after pool scale, re-run perf test and capture trace id. Also check prefill TTL and KV eviction thresholds — they were low for that pool.
Maddie: tests after scale — TTFTs look stable for 8/10 requests. A few outliers remain, sending trace id t_20260318_0930 for deep dive.
Kai: got trace, will check kernel selection logs and batching behavior. Quick ask — can you confirm they are not using a gateway that rewrites keepalive? gateway keepalive off can break affinity.
Maddie: confirmed gateway rewrites keepalive sometimes. We're asking customer to stop that.
Ben: also note security questionnaire asked about KMS for Dedicated. If we switch them we need KMS onboarding (2-week lead).
Maddie: ok ty — next steps: 1) ask customer to disable keepalive rewrite 2) enable client affinity and bump prefill to 128 for test 3) consider short Dedicated trial if they want SLA. I'll update them.
Kai: closing loop — if after affinity we still see >500ms TTFT for >5% requests, escalate to runtime team.
Li: adding a tiny follow-up: run `curl -H "x-request-id: r_..." https://console.redwood.ai/debug/tokens` and paste sample headers if you can.
Maddie: will do. thanks all :pray:
